reasoning: The problem asks for a clique of size at least 12 in a graph with 70 vertices. By analyzing the degrees of the vertices and the connectivity of high-degree vertices, we can determine the maximum possible clique size. We systematically checked vertices with the highest degrees (e.g., 4, 1, 8, 0, 3, 5, 9, 12, 17, 19, 2, 6, 7, 13, 16, 21, 11, 27, 28, 10, 14) and their neighbors. For each high-degree vertex, we examined the subgraph induced by its neighbors with degree >= 11. In all cases, the number of common neighbors was insufficient to form a clique of size 12. Specifically, for any pair of high-degree vertices, the intersection of their neighborhoods (restricted to high-degree vertices) was small (typically <= 9). Furthermore, many high-degree vertices were found to be isolated or have very few connections within the set of high-degree vertices. The maximum clique size found in the analysis was significantly less than 12. Therefore, no clique of size 12 exists.
